title: Close-coupling device (CCD)
scope_summary: The regulation approves close-coupling devices (CCDs), which automatically give extra clearance between towing vehicle and trailer bodies during articulation (Section I). It also approves vehicles of categories N2, N3, O3 and O4 with regard to the fitting of an approved CCD (Section II).
scope_quote: 1.1 This Regulation applies to vehicles of categories N2, N3, O3 and O4. ... 2.1.1 "Close-coupling device (CCD)" means a device which automatically provides sufficient space between the bodies of towing vehicles and trailers if additional clearance is needed during angular movement between them. Coupling devices having no adjusting effect on lengths and/or angles within the device are not covered by this Regulation;
applies_to_components: Parts required for installation and safe operation of a CCD (e.g. parts subject to towing and/or steering forces fixed to the chassis of the towing vehicle or trailer)
Fitting of an approved CCD on towing vehicles and trailers (trucks, tractors, trailers, semi-trailers, centre-axle trailers)
relation_to_other_regulations: The provided text does not state that R102 replaces, supersedes or is an alternative to any other UN Regulation.
Approval under Section II (vehicle) requires a CCD already approved under Section I of this same Regulation.
Approvals are granted under the 1958 Agreement concerning the Recognition of Approval for Motor Vehicle Equipment and Parts; approval number prefix 00 denotes the original series.

defined_terms.label: CCD
defined_terms.definition: A device which automatically provides sufficient space between the bodies of towing vehicles and trailers when additional clearance is needed during angular movement, excluding coupling devices with no adjusting effect on lengths and/or angles.

defined_terms.label: device approval
defined_terms.definition: Approval of a type of close-coupling device conforming to the requirements of Section I.

defined_terms.label: vehicle approval
defined_terms.definition: Approval of a vehicle with regard to the fitting of an approved close-coupling device.

defined_terms.label: vehicle type
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles not differing in CCD make/type, length and width, mass, CCD attachment points, vehicle description (truck, tractor, trailer, semi-trailer, centre-axle trailer) and steering equipment.

defined_terms.label: CCD type
defined_terms.definition: CCDs not differing in make and type, operating principle, means of attachment, overall dimensions at minimum and maximum extension, operating angle limits and kinematic characteristics relative to articulation angles.

defined_terms.label: automatic coupling
defined_terms.definition: A coupling procedure where reversing the towing vehicle against the trailer suffices to engage, secure and indicate proper engagement of the coupling without external intervention.

applicability_hints: Any coupling-related device that automatically varies length and/or angle (e.g. sliding/extending drawbar or kingpin/fifth-wheel shifting systems) to give body clearance during articulation is a CCD; fixed couplings with no adjusting effect are excluded.

Not only the CCD itself: all parts needed for its installation and safe operation, including chassis-fixed parts carrying towing and/or steering forces and the control systems, are subject to type approval.

Applies to both towing vehicles (N2, N3 trucks/tractors) and trailers (O3, O4 incl. semi-trailers and centre-axle trailers) – a trailer-mounted CCD or trailer steering equipment can trigger vehicle approval.
Changes to vehicle length/width, mass, CCD attachment points, or steering equipment (incl. auxiliary or trailer steering) define a new vehicle type under Section II.
Short-coupled combinations (e.g. car transporters, volume road trains) using extendable coupling systems are typical users.
